title: AI and the EU Digital Markets Act: Addressing the Risks of Bigness in Generative AI
venue: Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML)
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the policy problem of how to regulate the emergence of large, entrenched actors in generative AI markets. The authors argue that the European Union’s Digital Markets Act (DMA), which targets platform gatekeepers, does not explicitly cover generative AI services even though such services may become important gateways for business users and end users.

Rather than presenting an empirical study or educational intervention, the paper proposes a legal and regulatory framework for extending the DMA to generative AI. It discusses how generative AI can be offered as a platform service, identifies possible gatekeeper characteristics in the sector, and explains why computing power, early-mover advantage, data resources, and integrated systems could produce durable market power among a small number of firms.

The paper’s context is the EU digital regulatory environment, including the DMA and related AI governance efforts such as the AI Act. The authors conclude that certain generative AI services should be treated as core platform services and that some developers should be designated as gatekeepers, so that DMA obligations can support contestability, fairness, diversity, and innovation in generative AI markets.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual policy/opinion paper, not an empirical evaluation of an educational intervention. It contains no study design, no sample, and no measured outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper does not report any educational or student-level effects, so there is no measurable impact on K-12 outcomes.
